title: Gateway status endpoint (all services good)
hint: Run python/01_aap_api_health_check.py and check the failing service pods

title: Instance heartbeats current (ping)
hint: Stale heartbeat = instance lost; check the controller task pod logs

title: Instances ready with no health-check errors
hint: Run python/03_aap_instance_capacity_report.py; check instance errors in the UI

title: Subscription valid and compliant
detail: compliant=True, Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, Premium
hint: Renew or refresh the subscription manifest under Settings > Subscription

title: EDA status endpoint
hint: A slow or 500 response points at the EDA database/Redis; python/26_aap_eda_dispatcher_health_checker.py

title: Hub (Pulp) status: workers, content apps, DB, Redis
hint: Check the hub-worker / hub-content pods; python/21_aap_hub_sync_task_checker.py

title: Redis callback receiver queue
detail: callback_receiver_events_queue_size_redis. Red Hat: a large queue risks Redis running out of memory.
hint: Check Redis memory limits and the callback receiver; python/26_* dispatcher checker

title: Instance group capacity headroom
detail: Highest non-container instance group. Container groups are not capacity bound.
hint: Scale task replicas or raise task_resource_requirements limits; python/03_aap_instance_capacity_report.py

title: Job event processing lag
detail: callback_receiver_event_processing_avg_seconds. Red Hat: a large number means high lag; job output lags behind the job.
hint: Add task capacity / callback receiver workers; reduce verbosity

title: Managed hosts within subscription
hint: Delete stale hosts (host metrics) or expand the subscription

title: Job success rate (24h)
detail: Top failing: Deploy App (4), Patch Linux (1), Network Config Push (1)
hint: Run python/05_aap_stuck_job_finder.py and the job failure analyzer in the toolkit

title: No stuck pending jobs
hint: Pending jobs mean no capacity or a blocked dependency: python/05_aap_stuck_job_finder.py

title: Schedules firing on time
detail: no enabled schedule has a next_run in the past
hint: A next_run in the past means the dispatcher/scheduler is not running them

title: Enabled rulebook activations running
hint: python/24_aap_eda_activation_status_checker.py; check the activation-worker pods

title: Hub artifact storage free
hint: Expand the hub file-storage PVC or run orphan cleanup

title: Gateway API response time
hint: Check gateway pod CPU/memory and the database; see Performance considerations

title: Cleanup management jobs scheduled and passing
detail: job, activity stream, session and token cleanup scheduled
hint: Re-enable the default management job schedules; unbounded job events grow the database

title: Instance health checks recent
hint: Health checks run automatically; a stale one points at a stuck dispatcher

title: Inventory source syncs healthy
hint: Check cloud credentials / source plugins

title: No runaway jobs (> 4h)
hint: Set job template timeouts; python/05_aap_stuck_job_finder.py

title: Project syncs healthy
hint: Check SCM credentials and reachability from the task pods

title: No failed rulebook processes (24h)
hint: Inspect activation-instance logs

title: EDA project imports healthy
hint: Re-sync the project; check the SCM credential

title: Activations not restart-looping
hint: Review the rulebook process logs for the activation

title: No failed hub tasks (24h)
hint: python/21_aap_hub_sync_task_checker.py

title: Hub task queue draining
hint: Waiting tasks with workers online usually mean a stuck worker - restart hub-worker
